title: Desktop scanner replaces spectrophotometer for  low cost and  rapid  ELISA technique
protocol: Cut a white polypropylene sheet into a strip with dimensions of 9 cm in length and 3 cm in width.
Make an array of test zones on the strip by mildly hammering or pressing with a blunt end metal rod, ensuring each cavity is separated by 0.5 cm.
Pour FNAB solution (0.0625 mg/2.5 µl methanol/cavity) into each well of the PPµTP.
Allow slow evaporation of the solvent from the wells to coat them with FNAB.
Activate the dry coated plate by exposing it to UV light at a wavelength of 365 nm for 20 minutes.
Immobilize a capture molecule (anti-human IgG, anti-human IgE) onto the activated and untreated cavities of PPµTP.
Block any remaining reactive sites on the PPµTP cavities after immobilization of the capture molecules.
Bind analyte (human IgG or human IgE) to the capture molecule using ultrasound waves in a sonicator bath operating at 40 kHz with an output power of 120 W.
Wash the plates after each step to remove unbound substances.
Add 8 µl of substrate-dye buffer for color development.
Stop the reaction by adding 2 µl of 5% sulphuric acid.
Scan the PPµTP plate on a desktop scanner by placing it upside down.
Obtain the mean value of each R, G, and B from the scanned image in Adobe Photoshop.
Convert the RGB values to HSB using the Macbeth color calculator software.
Quantify the image as color saturation percentage.
